* ## The Role & Key Responsibilities
* **Job Title:** KW Sales Specialist

  **Location:** Hybrid, South West UK

  **Contract type and shift:** Permanent, Monday – Friday – 37.5 hours per week

  **Package includes** Salary from £50,000 (depending on experience) plus a benefits package designed to support your wellbeing and reward your impact, including performance related bonus, car allowance, private healthcare, and a matched pension contribution of up to 10%

  At KW, customer experience sits at the heart of everything we do. As part of the wider AsterraGroup, we’re proud to be one of the most progressive and forward-thinking feed businesses in the UK, combining national reach with genuine on-farm relationships.

  We are on the lookout for a KW On-Farm Sales Specialist to join our supportive and motivated sales team. This is a field-based role, working directly with dairy and beef farmers to deliver practical, credible solutions that help their businesses perform and thrive.

  What makes this role different is that we're versatile in our approach to background. If you bring previous experience in agricultural sales or on-farm operations, that’s great. If you do not have prior experience in agricultural sales or on-farm operations but can demonstrate a solid work ethic, curiosity about business practices in agriculture, and the tenacity required for a field-based sales role, we encourage your application.

  **The Role**

  Partnering with peers at KW and the extended Asterra business, you will take charge of a regional sales ledger, cultivating long-lasting, dependable relationships with farmers as you fulfill specified commercial targets.

  You will design and implement a comprehensive sales strategy tailored to the region, demonstrating the Asterra model in agricultural settings. Supported by technical, nutrition, customer service and marketing teams, you’ll offer tailored solutions rather than “off-the-shelf” products – always putting the customer first.

  This position involves a high level of initiative and personal responsibility. You’ll spend most of your time on farm, managing your own diary, spotting opportunities, and representing KW professionally within your territory and beyond.

  **What You’ll Be Doing:**

  + Building and managing a portfolio of dairy and beef customers, developing lasting, long-term relationships
  + Delivering against budget and contributing to the wider national sales plan
  + Creating and maintaining a strategic regional sales plan
  + Identifying new opportunities and feeding insight back into the wider business
  + Promoting the full KW / AB Agri ruminant offering, matching solutions to individual farm needs
  + Working closely with internal stakeholders across sales, technical, nutrition, marketing and customer service
  + Maintaining accurate CRM records to support effective customer service
  + Representing KW at farm visits, meetings, and relevant industry events

  **What you will bring:**

  + Demonstrated work ethic, professional approach, and self-motivation
  + Robust experience in customer engagement or consultative sales
  + The capacity to absorb new information efficiently and inquire thoughtfully
  + Comfort working with numbers, prices and margins
  + A genuine interest in agriculture and willingness to build technical knowledge over time
  + Credibility on farm and confidence engaging with farmers
  + An understanding of the key drivers of the UK ruminant sector

  Full technical training and ongoing support will be provided – what matters most is attitude, drive and commitment.

  **Practical Details:**

  + Field-based role with regular travel across the South West of the UK (Such as: Severn Estuary, Devon, Dorset, Hampshire, Wiltshire, Berkshire, Somerset, Gloucester, Oxfordshire, Herefordshire)
  + Full UK driving licence required
  + Monday–Friday, 8:30am–5:00pm (with flexibility inherent in on-farm work)
  + Budget responsibility for your own ledger

  **Where growth meets purpose**

  What sets us apart is how we delight our customers - and that’s because of great people like you.  People with different life experiences who share common values.  Together, we’re shaping a world where responsible nutrition is accessible to all. With a big goal comes equally big opportunities to make a career that truly feels like your own. As a team we’re collaborative, purpose-driven and encourage trying new ideas. We also find ways to nourish your individual journey, so everyone can feel proud of the difference that they make in their own way.

  We’re thrilled to share that AB Agri has been recognised as one of *The Times Top 50 Employers for Gender Equality 2025*.  This is a proud moment for us all. It highlights the real progress we’ve made to build a workplace that is inclusive, supportive, and fair for everyone.  Over the last 5 years we have rebuilt our talent management practices, from inclusive hiring, to transparent pay frameworks, flexible work, and the momentum of our Employee Network Groups.  Our actions are embedding inclusion at the heart of how we operate and creating a culture where people can be themselves

  As a Disability Confident employer, we’re committed to ensuring our application and recruitment processes work for everyone so if you need any additional support (like alternative formats for your application, bringing a support dog to the offices, a sign language interpreter - or anything else) just let us know.

* **Title**: Self-Employed Milk Sampler

  We’re looking for dedicated, self-employed Milk Samplers to join our team. This role offers the freedom to work across the beautiful countryside, visiting farms and collecting individual cow milk samples throughout the year.   **What you will be doing:**

  + Visiting dairy farms to collect milk samples
  + Organising sample pots in a numerical order to be sent to the Lab
  + Working directly with farmers and dairy herds
  + Following farm bio-security procedures
  + Travelling between farms within the area

  **Why You’ll Love This Role**:

  + Independence & Variety: Enjoy a mix of farm visits across the countryside.

  **What We’re Looking For**:

  + Valid driving licence & own transport
  + Organised and self-motivated individuals
  + An interest in farm life and dairy production

  As a self-employed contractor, you’ll have the autonomy to manage your work independently. Payment for this role is based on herd size, calculated on a per-cow basis, and we’ll discuss the details before you’re allocated to a farm/s.

# Software Engineer (UK)

## Role Details

Location

Fully Remote

Package

Salary dependent on experience + Benefits + Bonus

#### Role Overview

As a Software Engineer at Acceleraate, you will build across two fronts: the customer-facing platforms that deliver customer experience, and the internal tooling that powers our wider delivery team. The balance of that mix will shift over time, but the common thread is the same: well-architected, cloud-native software built on a serverless-first approach, where engineers take full ownership of what they deliver - from application code through to infrastructure.

Our AWS platform is well-established - CDK-managed, consistently structured across the estate, and set up to best practice from the ground up. We need someone who can operate at that standard, extend what we have thoughtfully, and bring genuine capability to new problems as they emerge.

You will work directly alongside our CTO and Engineering Director, both hands-on engineers. Decisions are made at engineering level. There is no lengthy approval chain between an idea and building it.

---

#### Why This Role is Exciting

* **Real breadth:** You'll work across customer-facing products, integration platforms, and internal tooling - often within the same sprint.
* **Strong foundations to build on:** Our AWS estate is serverless-first, CDK-managed, and built to best practice.
* **Integration at the core:** We connect Zoom's ecosystem with third-party platforms for real enterprise clients. The integration problems here are genuinely interesting.
* **POC to production:** We regularly evaluate new technologies to solve client problems. You'll be expected to pick things up, form a view, and prove it out.
* **AI as a real engineering tool:** We use AI actively as part of how we engineer, and we expect you to do the same.

---

#### What You Will Be Doing

##### Build and Extend Customer-Facing Platforms

A significant part of this role involves building and evolving the products our customers interact with directly. These are cloud-native, serverless applications - some greenfield, some established - and the work ranges from new feature development to architectural improvements as our customers' requirements grow.

You'll need to keep end users front of mind - the best technical decision and the right user experience don't always point in the same direction. Good engineering here means understanding the customer experience problem first, then building the right solution for it.

---

##### Design and Deliver Integrations

Integration is central to what Acceleraate does. You'll work with third-party APIs across a range of enterprise platforms - reviewing documentation, evaluating feasibility, and building robust integrations via our IntegrationHub platform.

There's real design work involved here. You'll need to think about failure modes, understand data flows end to end, and make sure things behave sensibly and are recoverable when something unexpected happens.

---

##### Own Your Infrastructure

Infrastructure is a core part of the engineering work here - it's defined and managed alongside the application code using AWS CDK across the application estate.

Our wider AWS governance layer - account structure, security controls, audit logging, and compliance guardrails - is managed via Terraform and built to best practice from the outset. You won't be in the weeds of that day to day, but you'll understand why it exists and what it gives us.

You'll operate within a GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline and an NX-managed monorepo. Understanding build pipelines, dependency graphs, and deployment strategies is part of the role, as is improving them when they're slowing things down.

---

##### Evaluate New Technologies and Drive POCs

We regularly encounter problems where the right solution isn't obvious, or where a new technology might open up a better approach. You'll be expected to pick things up, build something to test your thinking, form a view, and communicate it clearly.

---

##### Engineering with AI

We use AI tooling across the engineering team - for writing and reviewing code, exploring approaches, debugging, and generally moving faster. We expect you to do the same. That means being genuinely curious about the tools, using them regularly, and having the judgement to know when the output is good, when it's subtly wrong, and when AI isn't the right approach at all. You should understand the security and data implications of AI-assisted development, especially in customer-facing contexts, and be able to critically assess what's generated rather than just shipping it.

---

##### Contribute to Engineering Standards

You'll work with engineers who care as much about how things are built as whether they work. You're expected to engage seriously with code quality, consistency, and architectural decisions - raising concerns, asking the right questions, and contributing to how we build as much as what we ship. We've worked hard to keep the codebase in good shape and we'd like to keep it that way.

---

#### What We're Looking For

We're looking for an engineer with enough experience to know what good looks like - and enough drive to get there even when the problem is ambiguous. We value technical competence and self-direction over ticking every box.

##### Skills

* **TypeScript and Node.js:** Genuinely proficient - you know the ecosystem well, write clean well-typed code, and can apply patterns appropriately without over-engineering.
* **React:** Comfortable building real, production-grade UIs with meticulous attention to detail.
* **AWS Serverless:** Experience with Lambda, SQS, DynamoDB, EventBridge, Step Functions, and API Gateway - or a clear track record of picking up complex infrastructure paradigms quickly and correctly.
* **Infrastructure as Code:** Hands-on experience with AWS CDK, or the architectural understanding to learn it.
* **Third-party API integration:** Comfortable reading unfamiliar API documentation, evaluating feasibility, and building reliable integrations.
* **AI-assisted development:** Actively using AI tooling in your workflow, with the judgement to govern it.
* **Authentication & Authorisation:** Solid understanding of OAuth 2.0, token-based auth, and API security patterns - you've implemented these yourself rather than just consumed them.
* **Autonomous delivery:** Able to structure your own work, make sound decisions under uncertainty, and surface blockers early rather than quietly waiting them out.

##### Desirable

* Experience with GitHub Actions and CI/CD pipelines.
* Exposure to NX monorepo tooling.
* Familiarity with Terraform.
* Experience with Zoom APIs and SDKs.

---

#### Progression & Positioning

There's a clear growth path here into increasing architectural ownership - broader system design, more complex integration work, and the ability to lead specific product areas independently.

We are a growing team with an intentionally flat structure. Progression here is visible and earned on merit.

---

#### What We Offer

We believe in rewarding those who drive impact.

* **Bonus Scheme:** Discretionary performance-based bonus.
* **Growth Shares:** All employees receive Growth Shares so that you benefit from the company's future growth.
* **Generous Leave:** 28 days holiday plus public holidays.
* **Birthday Off:** Enjoy your birthday off every year.
* **Pension Plan:** 5% matched pension contribution.
* **Healthcare:** Private healthcare with Vitality.
* **Flexible Working:** Flexible hours and the option to work abroad for up to 20 days per year.
* **Life Events Leave:** Additional leave for major life moments.
* **Family Support:** Generous maternity/paternity/adoption policy.

---

#### How to Apply

Send a covering letter and CV to **careers@acceleraate.com** with the subject line **Software Engineer**.

Your covering letter must describe a technically challenging project or piece of engineering you have delivered (you don't need to name the client or employer). Please cover:

* The problem you were solving
* How you approached the technical design
* What you built including any key decisions
* The outcome, and anything you would do differently

Applications without the above will not be considered.

All applicants must have the existing right to live and work in the UK. Please note that this role is not eligible for visa sponsorship.

AI bots need not apply. No agencies please.

**Send your covering letter & CV to:** careers@acceleraate.com

Addepar is a global data and AI platform empowering investment professionals to turn complex financial information into actionable intelligence. Addepar unifies portfolio, market and client data in a total portfolio view and delivers AI-powered insights within investment and client workflows. More than 1,400 firms in nearly 60 countries use Addepar to manage and advise on nearly $9 trillion in assets. Its open platform integrates with nearly 650 software, data and consulting partners to power end-to-end investment operations across firms of all sizes and complexity. Addepar supports clients worldwide with offices in New York City, Salt Lake City, London, Edinburgh, Pune, Dubai, Geneva, Singapore and São Paulo.

#### **The Role**

This is not a behind-the-scenes support role—it is a highly visible, client-facing mandate designed for creative problem solvers. The Technical Success team provides premium services that enable business-as-usual (BAU) clients (RIAs, MFOs, Enterprises, SFOs, and Institutions) to expand value and accelerate growth after initial implementation. Technical Success Engineers are responsible for delivering high-value outcomes that align with client expectations, ensuring firms are using Addepar’s most up-to-date best practices and gold standard operating models.

In partnership with Client Success Managers, Account Executives, Support Analysts, and Product Managers, the Technical Success Engineer helps optimize clients’ overall experience and identify areas for R&D investment that lessen reliance on premium services. They are focused on identifying how Addepar can unlock significant value for clients’ businesses and regularly call upon their analytical skills in order to advise clients on how to model and examine their financial instruments and assets.

* Own and deliver high-value client outcomes aligned with client expectations, often requiring you to creatively navigate roadblocks and technical limitations.

This role is in support of Cencora's third party logistics service in Europe operating through our Alloga business.  
  
**Position Summary**

Cencora 3PL is replacing seven fragmented country IT stacks with a single pan-European platform spanning ERP, WMS, integration middleware, Client Portal, O2C and Analytics across 15 countries. This role owns the master data and entity governance foundations that determine whether that platform operates as a coherent system — or replicates the fragmentation it was designed to replace.

Sitting above-market and reporting to the VP Business Transformation, this is a strategic governance role, not a data maintenance function. You will define critical business entities, establish cross-market ownership structures and ensure data standards are agreed once and applied consistently — starting in Discovery and carrying through every subsequent rollout wave.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Define and govern the critical entity model across the full technology transformation scope — covering Client/Principal, End-Customer, Product/SKU, Location, Warehouse/Site, Carrier, Contract, Pricing, Service, Credit/Payment Terms, Licence/Compliance and Finance master data
* Establish a federated data ownership model — defining Business Owner, Data Steward and IT Owner per entity across O2C, Commercial, Finance, Operations, Quality and local markets
* Assess data readiness for O2C automation, Portal, Analytics and AI-enabled operations — translating gaps into integration assumptions, Business Case implications and sequencing constraints
* Differentiate and own the data dependency view for Client Portal and downstream customer portal(s) separately — preventing fragmented local data models from being hard-coded into a new strategic front end
* Work closely with IT Architecture and integration teams to define which entities must become reusable data services across ERP, WMS, Axway/Gateway, Portal and Analytics
* Provide decision-quality input to Design Authority and SteerCo — on entity ownership, golden record strategy, portal data architecture and integration assumptions
* Challenge local data exceptions constructively and hold the single-template principle across markets

.

**Candidate Requirements**

* Proven track record leading enterprise master data and entity governance in multi-country, multi-system environments — across customer, product, finance and logistics domains simultaneously
* Hands-on experience with golden record design, entity resolution, cross-reference/alias mapping and hierarchy management
* Ability to translate data gaps directly into business impact, integration effort, automation feasibility and Business Case assumptions
* Experience in ERP/WMS/CRM/portal/integration-heavy environments — D365 or SAP preferred; Axway or comparable middleware advantageous
* Strong stakeholder facilitation skills — able to drive ownership decisions across Commercial, Finance, IT and Operations without owning every downstream process
* Background in regulated industries — pharma, healthcare, logistics or life sciences preferred
* Comfortable building governance structure in environments with fragmented legacy systems, scarce SME capacity and high transformation pressure
* Bachelor's degree required; Master's preferred.
* 8+ years in enterprise data governance or MDM leadership.
* Fluent English required; additional European language advantageous

This role is available on a hybrid basis, attached to one of our 3PL in Europe.

**About Mars Veterinary Health Europe**

Mars Veterinary Health (MVH) Europe is a family of leading veterinary care providers committed to creating a better world for pets. Our network includes trusted brands such as AniCura and Linnaeus, operating over 500 animal hospitals and clinics across 17 European countries. Together, our teams deliver high-quality, modern veterinary care for companion animals, ensuring peace of mind for pet owners through excellent access and patient safety.

AniCura, our largest brand in Europe, provides care to over three million patients each year through 12,500 dedicated professionals. Linnaeus, operating primarily in the UK and Ireland, is home to over 6,000 Associates empowered to deliver exceptional care through a culture of collaboration, clinical excellence, and continuous development.

At MVH Europe, we prioritize a culture of accountability, inclusion, and wellbeing. We believe our purpose to make A BETTER WORLD FOR PETS starts with building a better world for our people. We support our teams through strong governance, comprehensive wellbeing programs, and a shared passion for delivering exceptional outcomes in veterinary care.

## About the role

We are looking for a **P&O Transformation Senior Analyst** to join the MVH Europe Transformation team for a 12-month fixed-term assignment.

MVH Global is driving an ambitious agenda focused on **standardisation, harmonisation and efficiency** across its global organisation. As part of this, MVH Europe is delivering a two-year transformation programme across seven business-critical programmes, helping shape how we work across Europe.

As a key member of the Transformation team, you will work across **P&O, Finance and Digital & Technology (D&T)**, providing the analysis and insight needed to understand the people and financial impact of transformation.

This is an exciting opportunity for an analytical and commercially minded professional who enjoys working with data, solving complex problems and partnering with stakeholders across a large, evolving organisation.

## 

## Roles and Responsibilities

You will take ownership of understanding and tracking the **people impacts of transformation** across the MVHE portfolio. This will include:

* Partnering with P&O Business Partners to identify and capture organisational changes arising from transformation initiatives.
* Tracking changes such as **role redesigns, promotions, lateral moves, redeployments and Associate exits**.
* Establishing and maintaining an accurate people-impact baseline across transformation workstreams.
* Analysing people data to identify trends, risks, opportunities and key insights.
* Producing clear and accurate reporting and management information for programme leadership and governance forums.
* Maintaining people-impact trackers and supporting documentation throughout the transformation lifecycle.
* Working closely with Finance Business Partners to understand the **cost and savings implications** of people changes.
* Supporting the Transformation Portfolio Lead and Transformation Finance Lead with **benefits tracking and realisation** across the portfolio.
* Identifying data gaps, inconsistencies and risks and proactively working with stakeholders to resolve them.
* Building strong relationships across P&O, Finance, D&T and transformation teams to ensure information is aligned and accurate.
* Supporting effective portfolio governance through high-quality data, reporting and analysis.

## Experience

We're looking for someone who combines strong analytical capability with excellent stakeholder skills and a genuine interest in how organisations change.

You will bring:

* Strong analytical skills and the ability to interpret complex information and turn it into meaningful insight.
* **Excellent Excel skills** and confidence working with large or complex datasets.
* Exceptional attention to detail and a strong focus on data accuracy and integrity.
* Experience working with reporting, management information, data analysis or transformation-related activities.
* Excellent organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with confidence engaging stakeholders at different levels.
* A collaborative and proactive approach to cross-functional working.
* Commercial awareness and an understanding of the financial implications of organisational change.
* The ability to work effectively in a fast-paced and changing transformation environment.
* A high level of discretion and professionalism when handling confidential people and organisational information.

Experience in **P&O/HR analytics, business analysis, finance, transformation, PMO, workforce planning or organisational change** would be highly relevant.

A Bachelor's degree in Business, Human Resources or a related discipline is desirable.

Department: Technical Placement

Description
The Commissioning Process Engineer will be responsible for planning, reviewing, coordinating and executing assigned commissioning activities and deliverables for a new build hydrogen production and storage facility. The role will support delivery of the commissioning execution plan to ensure that all process systems are commissioned safely, efficiently and in accordance with project requirements, client specifications, regulatory standards and industry best practice.
The successful candidate will report to the commissioning manger and will work closely with engineering, construction, operations and contractor teams throughout the commissioning phase to ensure successful delivery and handover of the plant.


Key Responsibilities
Writing, reviewing and updating client commissioning procedures, method statements and commissioning documentation.
Reviewing, commenting upon and approving contractor commissioning procedures to ensure compliance with project specifications, safety requirements and industry standards.
Verifying commissioning documentation including commissioning packs, check sheets, test records and handover dossiers.
Supporting systemisation, mechanical completion and turnover activities.
Coordinating process commissioning activities with engineering, construction, electrical, instrumentation and mechanical disciplines.
Participating in commissioning risk assessments, work co-ordination, and permit-to-work processes.
Ensuring commissioning activities comply with applicable health, safety and environmental requirements.
Supporting functional testing, integrated system testing and plant start-up.
Identifying commissioning issues and coordinating timely resolution with engineering and construction teams.
Recording commissioning progress and providing regular reports to the Commissioning Manager.
Supporting operator training and preparation of operational documentation where required.
Assisting with performance testing, reliability runs and final plant acceptance.
Supporting preparation of punch lists and close-out of commissioning actions.
Ensuring all commissioning records are complete and suitable for project handover.
Supporting the delivery of the commissioning plans and schedules.


Skills, Knowledge and Expertise
A minimum of five (5) years' experience in a commissioning role on industrial process plant projects. Experience in an operations engineering role will also be considered.
Demonstrable experience of commissioning process facilities, preferably within hydrogen, oil & gas, petrochemical, industrial gases, energy, or chemical processing industries.
Proven experience in reviewing, commenting upon and approving contractor commissioning procedures.
Proven experience in preparing, reviewing and updating client commissioning procedures and commissioning documentation.
Experience of working with, or leading, mechanical completion, systemisation, pre-commissioning, commissioning, start-up and performance testing activities.
Experience working within multidisciplinary project teams and coordinating commissioning activities with construction and operations personnel.
Experience supporting plant start-up and final handover to operations.

# Java Engineer (Core Settlement), RTGS Technology

## Job Description

**Java Engineer (Core Settlement), RTGS Technology**

**Location: Leeds**

**Job Description**

This is an opportunity to take a senior engineering role inside one of the UK’s most critical technology environments.

RTGS settles on average £800bn per day and is Critical National Infrastructure. The Core Settlement team owns the software at the heart of that service - including the core settlement engine and the services responsible for transaction processing, settlement behaviour, and financial state across RTGS.

As a Java Engineer in the Core Settlement team, you will build, operate, and continuously improve the Java services that underpin RTGS settlement. You will work independently on meaningful pieces of work, take clear ownership of what you deliver, and be expected to bring your own engineering judgement to the problems in front of you.

This team follows a “you build it, you own it model”. You are responsible not just for delivering software, but for how it performs in production - diagnosing issues, restoring service, and turning operational learning into engineering improvements

**Flexible Working Options**

This role is open to flexible working patterns, which may include:

* Flexible start and end times to each day
* A 50% in-office attendance requirement that can be spread across the month, with flexibility to reflect operational commitments such as on-call activity
* There will be some occasional out-of-hours activity to support production releases and change testing, which may include limited weekend or non-core hours working
* Working from abroad (subject to approval)

**Opportunities in Leeds:**

We’re excited to be growing our presence in Leeds, a city we’ve been connected to for nearly 200 years! Our modern, accessible office in the City Centre offers a supportive, flexible working environment. The majority of roles, including this one, are now available in Leeds, giving you the chance to build a meaningful career outside of London while contributing to our mission from a dynamic and growing location. You’ll work collaboratively with London-based colleagues in a hybrid model, with regular opportunities to travel into the London office to meet and connect together in person.

**A day in the role:**

Your day might begin with the team stand-up - reviewing priorities, surfacing blockers, and agreeing what the team focuses on next.

Most of your day will be writing Java - implementing a change to the settlement engine, fixing a defect in transaction processing, or improving how a service handles failure and recovers. You will be writing tests alongside the code, not as a separate step.

You will contribute to code reviews on both sides - giving considered, useful feedback on others’ work and engaging constructively with feedback on your own. At this level, code review is a place where you add value, not just receive it.

When something goes wrong in production, you will be part of the response - diagnosing issues, supporting service restoration, and making sure the underlying problem is properly addressed. You bring enough experience to engage meaningfully, not just observe.

This role includes participation in an on-call rota. When on call, you are part of the team responsible for the services in production - responding to incidents, supporting diagnosis and recovery, and making sure lessons learned feed back into the codebase.

In addition, you will support planned change activity outside of core hours where required, including release deployment and testing, to meet the needs of a high-availability service.

**Role Requirements:**

As a Java Engineer in the Core Settlement team, you will be an active contributor responsible for delivering and operating core application services.

You will:

* Build and operate Java-based settlement services, taking ownership of the work you pick up and seeing it through from implementation to production
* Write clean, well-tested code - with unit, integration, and component tests as a natural part of delivery, not an afterthought
* Take part in code reviews - contributing feedback and applying the same discipline to your own code
* Engage with solution designs and technical direction, applying your own engineering judgement to implementation and raising concerns before they become problems
* Support production services - participating in on-call, helping to diagnose and resolve incidents, and ensuring issues lead to real improvements
* Develop your understanding of how the services you work on behave under load, failure, and recovery scenarios
* Work within change management and governance processes appropriate for a regulated, high-availability environment
* Contribute to a culture of continuous improvement within the tea

Minimum Criteria 

We are looking for someone who has the following key skills and experience:

* Good Java engineering experience building and supporting backend services
* Experience working with relational databases (e.g. Oracle, PL/SQL)
* Experience with distributed systems, service-to-service interactions or event-driven patterns (e.g. Kafka)
* Familiarity with container platforms (e.g. OpenShift)
* Experience working with live systems, including troubleshooting and debugging issues
* A solid testing discipline (unit and integration testing)
* Understanding of how software behaves in production (failure modes, recovery, operational risk)

Essential Criteria

We are interested in hearing from candidates who demonstrate the following:

* Experience building and supporting backend Java services in a team environment
* Experience contributing to the design and implementation of service-based systems
* Experience supporting production systems, including participation in incident response
* Understanding of performance considerations in Java services (latency, throughput, memory, concurrency)
* Practical awareness of secure coding practices
* Ability to work closely with engineers, designers and stakeholders
* A track record of delivering code into production and supporting it over time
* High levels of integrity, organisation and self‐motivation, with a desire for self‐improvement
* Typically 3–5 years’ experience working with backend Java services

 

Desirable Criteria

It would also be beneficial, though not essential, to have some of the following:

* Frontend technologies (e.g. React, TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML, CSS)
* Messaging and streaming platforms (e.g. Kafka) beyond basic familiarity
* Testing frameworks and approaches (e.g. Jest, service-based testing)
* Build and tooling (e.g. Gradle, Jenkins, Git/GitHub)
* Experience with Oracle database-backed applications
* Experience working in Agile environments (e.g. SAFe)
* Financial services, payments, settlement systems, or other regulated / high-availability environments

Don’t hesitate to apply if you don’t meet all of the criteria. We value diverse perspectives and believe different experiences lead to stronger teams and better outcomes.

RTGS Technology is moving to a product engineering model, with teams aligned to business and platform domains. The Core Settlement team sits at the heart of that model, owning the services responsible for settlement processing, settlement logic and transaction lifecycle execution within RTGS.

As a Java Engineer in this team, you will contribute directly to the safety, resilience, and correctness of some of the most critical software in the UK financial system. #### Job Description

**Head of** **PMO – HVDC Projects**

**Location: Edinburgh Park Office – with flexible hybrid working and occasional travel throughout the UK.**

**Salary: from £76,800 - £96,000 per annum plus up to 30% annual bonus, £450pcm car allowance and family healthcare**

**Full-time | Permanent**

**Closing Date: 7th September 2026**

**Create a better future, quicker!**

At SP Energy Networks, we're delivering one of the UK's most ambitious infrastructure programmes, investing over £12 billion in Scotland's transmission network by 2031 to support the transition to a low-carbon future.

We're seeking an experienced **Head of PMO** to shape and lead the Project Management Office (PMO) across our growing HVDC portfolio, including nationally significant projects such as Eastern Green Link 1, Eastern Green Link 4 and Western Link 2. These projects are critical to strengthening energy security, enabling renewable generation at scale and accelerating the UK's journey to Net Zero.

This is a rare opportunity to build and develop a best-in-class PMO function supporting some of the country's most significant energy infrastructure projects. You'll lead across a portfolio of complex, multi-billion pound programmes while establishing the people, processes, governance and systems that will drive successful delivery for years to come.

Working closely with senior leaders, Joint Venture partners and delivery teams, you'll influence how major projects are governed and delivered, creating a lasting impact on the future of the UK's energy network.

If you're passionate about major projects, transformational leadership and building high performing teams, we'd love to hear from you.

**What You'll Be Doing**

As **Head of PMO**, you'll lead the PMO function across the HVDC portfolio, including direct oversight of PMO delivery for Western Link 2, while helping shape a best-in-class capability across all HVDC projects.

You'll manage a growing team of PMO and Project Controls professionals across multiple UK locations, driving governance, reporting, planning and performance management while developing capability and supporting future portfolio growth.

**Key responsibilities will include:**

* Leading, developing and expanding the HVDC PMO team, including recruitment, capability building and performance management.
* Playing a key role in the development and evolution of the PMO function, establishing best-practice standards, processes and governance frameworks across the portfolio.
* Creating a consistent approach to project controls, enabling collaboration, scalability and shared learning across major projects.
* Working closely with Joint Venture partners, contractors and internal stakeholders to ensure effective PMO capability throughout the project lifecycle.
* Overseeing planning and scheduling, governance, reporting, risk management, change control and document management activities.
* Driving the adoption of digital tools and data-led decision making, including Power BI, Primavera P6, CEMAR and other project controls systems.
* Supporting executive reporting, regulatory submissions and portfolio performance reviews.
* Championing continuous improvement, innovation and lessons learned to enhance delivery performance across the HVDC programme.
* Establishing and embedding governance and assurance frameworks that support successful project delivery while driving consistency across the portfolio.
* Influencing the future development of project controls, PMO capability and digital transformation across HVDC projects.

**What You'll Bring**

We're looking for an experienced PMO and project controls leader with a proven track record of delivering major infrastructure programmes. You'll be a strategic leader who can influence outcomes, solve complex challenges and drive continuous improvement, while helping to build and shape a high-performing PMO function across a growing portfolio of nationally significant projects.

**You'll bring:**

* Significant experience leading PMO, project controls or programme management functions within large-scale infrastructure, engineering, construction, energy or EPC environments.
* Proven success in building, developing and leading high-performing multidisciplinary teams.
* Strong knowledge of governance, project controls, reporting, risk, change management and project assurance.
* Experience working within NEC4 and/or FIDIC contract environments on major capital projects.
* A recognised project management qualification (APM, PRINCE2 or equivalent) or substantial relevant experience.
* Excellent stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the ability to engage effectively at all levels.
* Strong commercial awareness and understanding of contractual processes and project delivery best practice.
* Experience using project controls and digital tools such as Power BI, Primavera P6, CEMAR, BIM, ACC or similar.
* Excellent communication, analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to provide clear insights and navigate complex challenges.
* A collaborative leadership style, resilience and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced, evolving environment.

**You'll stand out if you have:**

* Experience within transmission, utilities, energy or other nationally significant infrastructure projects.
* Experience establishing, building or transforming PMO functions.
* Portfolio-level governance and reporting experience across multiple concurrent projects.
* A passion for innovation, continuous improvement and modern project controls practices.

**What’s in it for you**

As well as a competitive salary which is reviewed annually, you can also enjoy a number of other benefits. With our pension scheme, we’ll double match your contribution up to a company contribution of 10%.

At ScottishPower, we believe it’s the little things we do in life that make a big difference. From helping you look after your family’s wellbeing, save for your future and take personal steps for climate action – our benefits are designed to help you do just that -  so that you have everything you need to take care of your world – today and tomorrow.

That’s why our benefits include:

* 36 days annual leave

* Holiday purchase – perfect your work/life balance with extra annual leave

* Share Incentive Plan and Sharesave Scheme

* Payroll giving and charity matched funding

* Technology Vouchers – save more and spread the cost of your technology purposes

* Count us in – pledge to reduce carbon emissions and help fight climate change

* Electric Vehicle Schemes – to help you transition to green/clean driving

* Cycle to Work scheme and public transport season ticket loans

* Options to purchase dental insurance, private medical insurance, health cash plan and annual health assessments

* Life Assurance (4x salary)

* Access to ‘nudge’ financial wellbeing support

* Plus shopping, leisure, restaurant and gym discounts, and unique employee deals on travel insurance and more

**Why SP Energy Networks**

SP Energy Networks is part of the Iberdrola Group, one of the world’s largest integrated utility companies and a world leader in wind energy. We keep electricity flowing to homes and businesses through Central and Southern Scotland, North Wales and in the North West of England. We operate over 4000km of cables and lines that make-up the transmission network – connecting infrastructure like wind farms into the electricity system. It’s a role that puts us right at the heart of Scotland’s ambition to be Net Zero by 2044. And we’re taking it very seriously.

With diverse opportunities across our businesses and a commitment to invest in our own internal talent, ScottishPower can offer people real career opportunities that meet personal and professional goals, in a global organisation.

Inclusion, diversity, and a social purpose are at the heart of everything we do. Together with our values, they bring us together into a stronger, more sustainable business with direct links to the communities we serve. It takes all kinds of people to build a large-scale business like ours, so whatever your background, you’ll fit right in.

# UK & US Master’s Applications-UK & US Master’s Applications

**Location:** London **Working pattern:** Hybrid -3 days per week in the London office **Employment:** Full-time **Salary**: £50,000–£65,000 base salary, plus performance-based bonus

**About Blue Education**

Blue Education is a premium education and university admissions consultancy supporting ambitious students applying to leading universities in the UK, US and around the world.

We provide highly personalised university admissions guidance, academic mentoring and long-term educational planning. Our team includes graduates and educators from Oxford, Cambridge, Ivy League and other world-leading universities, and we work with academically strong students seeking admission to highly competitive programmes.

As our postgraduate admissions work continues to grow, we are looking for an experienced Graduate Admissions Consultant to work directly with students applying primarily for Master’s programmes in the UK and US.

**The Role**

This is a hands-on admissions consulting and mentoring position.

You will work one-to-one with students throughout the postgraduate application journey: helping them decide what and where to study, assess their competitiveness, strengthen their profile, develop an application strategy and present their academic and professional experience convincingly.

A significant part of the role involves providing detailed, substantive guidance on application materials. You will work closely with students on the content, structure, academic narrative, programme fit and positioning of their applications, often across multiple drafts.

We are looking for someone who enjoys working closely with students and has the judgement, experience and communication skills to provide exceptional postgraduate admissions guidance.

**What You Will Do**

**1. Application Strategy & Programme Selection**

Develop an individual postgraduate admissions strategy for each student based on their academic background, interests, experience and longer-term goals.

* Assess students’ academic records, research, internships, professional experience and extracurricular activities.
* Understand their academic interests and career ambitions.
* Help students clarify what they should study when they are considering different subjects or directions.
* Research and recommend appropriate Master’s programmes in the UK and US.
* Develop ambitious but realistic university and programme lists.
* Assess how competitive a student is for individual programmes.
* Explain how different programmes and admissions committees are likely to evaluate their profile.
* Identify weaknesses or gaps in their candidacy and recommend practical ways to address them.
* Develop a coherent overall strategy connecting the student’s previous experience, current interests and future ambitions.

You should be able to explain not simply where a student should apply, but why a particular programme fits them and what they need to do to become a stronger candidate.

**2. Student Mentoring & Profile Development**

Build strong one-to-one mentoring relationships with students throughout their postgraduate application journey.

For students who begin working with Blue Education before the application cycle, you may advise on areas including:

* Academic development and course selection;
* Further reading and independent academic work;
* Research opportunities;
* Internships and professional experience;
* Relevant extracurricular activities;
* Relationships with potential academic referees;
* GRE or GMAT preparation where appropriate;
* Broader academic and career direction.

You will meet students regularly, review their progress and adapt their strategy as their profile and ambitions develop.

Our objective is to help students become stronger applicants, not simply complete an application process.

**3. Detailed Guidance on Application Materials**

Provide detailed, hands-on advice on the content and positioning of students’ application materials.

These may include:

* Statements of Purpose;
* Personal Statements;
* Academic and professional CVs;
* Supplementary essays and application questions;
* Recommendation strategy;
* Research proposals where relevant;
* Scholarship applications.

You will work with students through multiple drafts and provide specific, actionable feedback on both what they are saying and how they are positioning themselves.

**You will help students:**

* Identify the academic, research, professional and extracurricular experiences most relevant to their application.
* Decide what should be emphasised, developed, reduced or removed.
* Build a coherent narrative connecting their previous experience, current academic interests and future goals.
* Articulate intellectual interests with sufficient depth and specificity.
* Explain convincingly why they want to pursue a particular programme.
* Demonstrate meaningful programme fit.
* Position research, internships, employment and other experiences effectively.
* Select appropriate evidence and examples to support the claims they make.
* Address changes in academic direction or unusual aspects of their profile where necessary.
* Improve the logic, coherence and overall persuasiveness of the application.
* Ensure that different parts of the application reinforce one another.

You should be comfortable identifying weak arguments, underdeveloped examples, unclear motivations and ineffective positioning, and giving students detailed guidance on how to improve them. The emphasis is on close engagement with the substance of each application and feedback that materially improves the student’s thinking, positioning and final submission.

**4. Application Management & Interview Preparation**

Guide students through the complete postgraduate application process.

This includes:

* Developing application timelines and priorities.
* Monitoring university and programme deadlines.
* Ensuring students understand programme-specific requirements.
* Advising on referee selection and recommendation strategy.
* Reviewing the overall consistency and readiness of applications before submission.
* Helping students manage overlapping deadlines and changing application plans.
* Preparing students for postgraduate admissions interviews where required.

Interview preparation may involve mock interviews, discussion of academic interests and previous research, challenging students on their motivations and conducting practice with unfamiliar or difficult questions. The aim is to help students communicate their ideas with greater clarity, confidence and intellectual depth.

**Who We Are Looking For**

We are looking for someone with strong academic credentials, excellent admissions judgement and meaningful professional experience supporting competitive postgraduate applications.

**Essential Requirements**

**Academic Background**

A degree from a highly selective, globally leading university is required.

We are particularly interested in graduates of:

* Oxford or Cambridge;
* Ivy League universities;
* Stanford;
* MIT;

or institutions of comparable international academic standing and selectivity.

A postgraduate degree is advantageous but not essential.

**Professional Experience**

* Approximately 3–5 years of directly relevant experience in postgraduate admissions consulting, university admissions advising or high-level education consulting.
* Substantial experience supporting students applying to competitive Master’s programmes.
* Strong knowledge of both UK and US postgraduate admissions.
* Experience advising applicants targeting highly selective universities and programmes.
* Admissions Judgement
* You should be able to look at a student’s profile and form a clear independent view about:
* Which programmes genuinely suit them;
* Where they should apply;
* Which options are realistic and where they could be more ambitious;
* What is missing from their profile;
* How they can strengthen their candidacy;
* Which experiences should form the centre of their application;
* How they should position themselves to an admissions committee.

We are looking for strong professional judgement and the ability to develop genuinely individualised strategies for each student.

**Communication & Mentoring**

**You should have:**

* Excellent written and spoken English.
* Strong one-to-one mentoring skills.
* The confidence to challenge ambitious students constructively.
* The ability to explain complicated admissions decisions clearly.
* Strong analytical reading skills.
* The ability to give detailed, specific and actionable feedback on written applications.
* Strong interpersonal skills when working with students and, where appropriate, their families.

**Organisation & Ownership**

You should be highly organised, reliable and detail-oriented, with the ability to manage multiple applications and deadlines simultaneously.

You will be expected to take ownership of individual student cases and work independently while maintaining consistently high standards.

**Nice to Have**

The following would be advantageous:

* Experience advising on MBA applications.
* Familiarity with leading UK, US and European MBA programmes.
* Knowledge of GMAT and GRE requirements.
* Experience with research-intensive Master’s applications.
* Experience supporting applicants across a range of academic disciplines.
* Experience studying or working in both the UK and US.
* Experience working with international students.
* Mandarin Chinese language ability.
* Experience working with Chinese students or families.

**What Success Looks Like**

A successful Graduate Admissions Consultant will:

* Develop thoughtful, individualised application strategies.
* Build trusted relationships with students and provide clear, honest advice.
* Help students make better decisions about what and where to study.
* Identify weaknesses early enough for students to address them.
* Provide detailed, actionable guidance that materially improves application content and positioning.
* Maintain high standards across multiple student cases and application deadlines.
* Receive strong feedback from students and families.
* Contribute to strong admissions outcomes at highly selective universities.

The best consultants do more than improve the final application. They help students understand what makes them a compelling candidate and how to communicate that convincingly.

**Why Join Blue Education?**

You will work with ambitious students targeting some of the world’s most competitive postgraduate programmes and have the opportunity to engage deeply with their academic decisions, application strategies and written materials.

**Blue Education offers:**

* £50,000–£65,000 base salary plus performance-based bonus;
* High-touch, intellectually engaging student work;
* The opportunity to focus on postgraduate admissions consulting and develop deep expertise in the field;
* An academically strong international team;
* Hybrid working, with three days per week in our London office;
* Professional development opportunities;
* Company pension and other UK employee benefits.

Some flexibility may occasionally be required during peak application periods or when supporting students across international time zones.

If you have strong postgraduate admissions experience, enjoy working closely with ambitious students and take pride in giving detailed, thoughtful and academically rigorous advice, we would like to hear from you.

Service Desk Engineer

Role: Service Desk Engineer

Location: Remote

Salary: up to £45k based on experience, plus benefits

About Charles Square

Charles Square (CSq) is a Technology Services Partner serving the financial sector and regulated businesses. CSq provides Enterprise Support, Security, Strategy and Supply solutions that set a high bar on reliability, security, and customer experience.

CSq is an agile company, ISO27001 certified and a Microsoft Partner. Our goal is to help companies transform and innovate using technology.

Working for CSq will give you first-hand access to world class technologies, exciting new applications, bespoke software products, fantastic clients, and a great team.

Role Outline

We are looking for an experienced, customer-focused and enthusiastic Service Desk Engineer to join our team. You will provide support for on-premises and Azure environments for our customers.

You should have a genuine interest in solving IT issues and be empathetic to customer needs and requirements. Day to day tasks include management and troubleshooting of customer environments and working with our project delivery team to plan and deploy environments and services for our customers.

Your time will be spent as a point of contact for our service desk, dealing with critical tickets and escalations, including change management. The candidate should be prepared to split their working day between providing support for customer environments and colleagues, delivery and documentation.

You should possess excellent written and verbal communication skills, be willing to collaborate with the wider IT support teams and help us continue to develop a strong partnership with our customers.

Key Responsibiltis 

Reporting to the Service Desk Manager and working as part of a team of four engineers, you will:

* Act as the technical point of contact for incidents and service requests
* Lead troubleshooting across Azure and on-premises infrastructure, taking ownership of major incidents from triage through to resolution and post-incident review
* Drive root cause analysis on recurring or high-impact issues and implement permanent fixes rather than repeated workarounds
* Review and implement changes within customer environments, acting as a technical reviewer for changes raised by other engineers
* Build and maintain technical documentation, runbooks and knowledge base articles to reduce future escalations and uplift the wider team
* Identify opportunities where additional CSq services could genuinely benefit a customer, and flag these to account management

 

What you will need to succeed

For this role we are looking for someone with previous experience in an IT Solution Provider or MSP environment, with in-depth knowledge in troubleshooting and the hunger to learn and progress as well as bringing something special to the company.

* Experience supporting and troubleshooting complex environments.
* Ability to work in a fast-paced environment and manage competing priorities.
* Ability to prioritise and self-manage your workload.
* You will have excellent client service skills, dealing with time critical issues efficiently as well as being enthusiastic about expanding your technical knowledge.

  

Required Skills

* Microsoft AZ-104 certification (or equivalent demonstrable experience); VMware Certified Professional is desirable
* 4+ years’ experience in a similar role
* Demonstrable working knowledge across most of the following Azure and on-premises components: VMware, Active Directory, Exchange (Online and/or on-premises), Intune, Conditional Access, and Storage/SAN

Working Pattern

This is a remote role.

This role operates on a shift basis, Monday to Friday. Shifts are scheduled to provide coverage across our operating window of 07:00 to 23:00, and you will be allocated to a shift pattern within these hours. Shift times are subject to a published rota and may vary to meet business needs.

Applicants must have the right to work in the UK; visa sponsorship is not available for this role.

We have an exciting opening for a Junior Print Designer to join us at Renfold. This role is ideally suited to an established Assistant Print Designer who is ready to take the next step, or a Junior Print Designer looking to broaden their experience in a fast-moving, multi-brand environment.

You will help curate commercially relevant ranges and develop original print across our multi-gender, off-price brands and collections, spanning fashion, home and accessories across Ladies, Mens and Kids.

We are looking for someone who can help build, shape and accelerate our emerging fashion brands, balancing trend and newness with strong commercial awareness. This is an ideal role for someone with creative instincts, initiative and the ability to execute quickly and resourcefully.

You will report to the Senior Designer and work as part of a small, growing team. This is a full-time, permanent role with flexi-hours. The role is office-based during probation, followed by hybrid working with three office days per week after successful completion of probation. Salary is competitive and dependent on experience.

# Role Overview

As Junior Print Designer, you will play a key role in creating trend-inspired, elevated and commercially relevant prints that reflect each brand's identity and customer.

Working closely with the Senior Designer, Commercial Manager and wider cross-functional teams, you will support the development of cohesive ranges from initial research and concept through to production-ready artwork and approval. You will manage defined print briefs and smaller areas of the range independently, while receiving support and development as you take on greater ownership.

Success in the role will mean delivering commercially relevant print options on brief and on time; producing accurate, production-ready artwork and approval comments; maintaining organised print libraries and trackers; and building strong working relationships with internal teams, customers and suppliers.

# Key Responsibilities

* **Trend & Market Strategy and Analysis:** Conduct ongoing trend, competitor and market research to inform seasonal print direction and maintain commercial relevance. Create clear visual presentations and confidently share ideas with the design team and senior stakeholders.
* **Print Design and Development:** Create original, commercially relevant prints using hand-drawn, painted and digital techniques. Develop seamless repeats, placements, engineered prints and colourways appropriate to the product, customer and price point.
* **Drive Newness in Print and Range Curation:** Work with the Senior Designer and Commercial Manager to curate cohesive, seasonally appropriate ranges that balance trend, newness, customer needs and proven commercial print handwriting.
* **Decipher Print Trends:** Identify and prioritise the key print directions and commercial print stories that will drive the seasonal assortment across the relevant brands and categories.
* **Production-Ready Artwork and Approvals:** Prepare accurate artwork, CADs, colourways, specifications and print information for sampling and production, including Pantone references where required. Support strike-off, lab-dip and sample approvals, ensuring colour, scale and design intent are maintained throughout development.
* **Collaboration & Cross-Functional Relationships:** Partner closely with commercial, design and buying, colleagues to align print and design decisions with customer, cost, quality and delivery requirements.
* **Technical and Administrative Support:** Produce print and shape tech packs, assist in fit and sample review sessions, maintain organised artwork and print libraries, support approvals and prepare for customer and internal meetings.
* **Supplier Communication:** Communicate effectively with global factories and suppliers, responding promptly to queries and supporting the resolution of technical or production issues.
* **Fabric & Sustainability:** Apply a practical understanding of fabrications, print techniques and production limitations. Support the selection of options that meet sustainability, quality and price requirements while driving newness.
* **Workflow Management:** Manage allocated briefs and approvals against the critical path, maintain accurate trackers and files, and communicate progress, risks and changes clearly to the wider team.
* An established Assistant Print Designer ready to step into a Junior role, or experience at Junior Print Designer level.
* A strong portfolio demonstrating original print development, hand-drawing and painting techniques, digital design, repeat patterns, colourways and commercial application.
* Strong proficiency in Adobe Photoshop and Illustrator, with confident CAD skills and the ability to work accurately at pace.
* Experience creating seamless repeats and preparing production-ready print artwork and specifications.
* A good understanding of colour, scale, placement, Pantone references, print techniques and how artwork translates across different products and fabrications.
* Strong commercial awareness and an understanding of how brand identity and customer needs inform print and range decisions.
* Good knowledge of brand identity and experience working across multiple brands at the same time.
* Excellent organisation and time-management skills, with the ability to balance multiple briefs, projects and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
* Clear communication and collaborative working skills, including confidence presenting ideas and communicating with suppliers.
* A proactive, resourceful approach and willingness to contribute across creative, technical and administrative tasks.
* Experience within off-price retail or a fast-paced supplier, retailer or multi-brand environment would be advantageous.
* Experience working across fashion, experience in home and/or accessories would be advantageous.

**Role Summary**

We are seeking an experienced administrator and coordinator to join our Property & Buildings Team. This is a varied role focused on committee administration, case management, stakeholder liaison, governance support and maintaining compliance within a structured decision-making process. Full training will be provided on the Church of England's faculty system and relevant legislation. We are particularly interested in candidates with strong administrative, governance, coordination or case management experience.

Providing support for the work of the Diocesan Advisory Committee (DAC) - A group of experts that advises churches on building works, changes, and care to ensure they are appropriate, sustainable, and compliant -

 and the Diocese of Liverpool’s closed church buildings processes. The role is key to ensuring the smooth, efficient, and compliant operation of DAC procedures, while supporting parishes in the care, development, and sustainable use of church buildings and churchyards.

Working closely with senior diocesan staff, Archdeacons, and national Church of England bodies, the postholder will act as a primary point of contact for parishes, clergy, and external stakeholders. They will facilitate faculty processes (similar to secular planning system), manage communications and records, and provide guidance on heritage, legal, and planning matters – which is something we can provide support and training on. Through strong organisational skills and a proactive approach, the role supports the Diocese of Liverpool’s commitment to responsible stewardship, effective mission, and long-term sustainability, working with and advising parishes to develop successful applications.

**We'd Love to Hear From You If You Have Experience In:**

* Public sector administration and business support
* Committee or governance administration
* Casework or process management
* Compliance or regulatory environments
* Property, housing or planning administration
* Project coordination
* Legal support or paralegal work
* Stakeholder engagement and customer service

**Duties and key responsibilities:**

1. **DAC Coordination & Committee Management**
   * Coordinate the overall operation of the Diocesan Advisory Committee and its subcommittees
   * Prepare agendas, reports, and papers for meetings
   * Attend meetings, take minutes, and communicate decisions and advice
   * Maintain records of DAC business, including the faculty register
   * Manage conflicts of interest and ensure governance standards are met
   * Circulate agendas, minutes, and documentation to relevant stakeholders
   * Represent the DAC at hearings, including consistory court when required
   * Present applications to the DAC
2. **Faculty Process & Advisory Support**
   * Act as the first point of contact for all faculty-related enquiries
   * Provide guidance on the care and maintenance of church buildings and churchyards
   * Support clergy, PCCs, and parish officers in navigating the faculty system
   * Assist with applications and documentation via the Online Faculty System
   * Manage expectations regarding processes, requirements, and timescales
   * Work closely with Archdeacons on faculty matters and permissions
   * Work independently within delegated responsibilities to support and progress faculty applications, providing practical guidance and ensuring processes are followed appropriately.
3. **Stakeholder Engagement & Communication**
   * Build effective relationships with parishes, clergy, architects, surveyors, and local authorities
   * To coordinate education within the diocese of the care and development of church buildings
   * Liaise with national bodies such as the Church Buildings Council and Historic England-
   * Collaborate with internal diocesan teams, including Net Zero and Mission & Pastoral
   * Deliver guidance and support to new incumbents and parish representatives
   * To attend the annual meeting for DAC Secretaries and Chairs organised by the Church Buildings Council
4. **Church Buildings Development & Stewardship**
   * Support parishes in developing proposals for building changes and improvements
   * Promote sustainable, accessible, and mission-aligned use of church buildings
   * Maintain awareness of planning regulations and conservation requirements
   * Encourage best practice in building care, sustainability, and accessibility
   * Receive and review Quinquennial Inspection Reports, working closely with the Archdeacon to support parishes in delivering recommended repairs and maintenance works.
5. **Administration, Data & Systems**
   * Maintain accurate records for church buildings, applications, and inspections
   * Ensure documentation is up to date, accessible, and compliant
   * To maintain a register of architects and surveyors approved to undertake quninquennial inspection reports in the diocese
   * Use digital systems (e.g., Online Faculty System) effectively
6. **Mission & Pastoral Support (Closed Churches)**
   * Support the Closed Church Buildings (Uses and Disposals) sub-committee
   * Prepare agendas and minutes for meetings
   * Assist with administration of closed church buildings
   * Facilitate access for inspections and works, including liaising with stakeholders
   * Gather and manage utility and property-related information
7. **Compliance & Governance**
   * Ensure legal and procedural compliance under ecclesiastical legislation
   * Maintain indemnity insurance arrangements for DAC members
   * Support governance processes, reporting, and audits
   * Keep informed of relevant legislation, policies, and sector developments

This role will form an integral part of the Property & Buildings Team, providing support to the Team and parishes and undertaking responsibilities as otherwise directed.

Who we are:

Constructive Bio is a growing Cambridge based biotechnology company built on a simple conviction: the molecules that matter most are often the ones that can’t yet be made.

We’ve rewritten the genetic code give cells access to new ncAA chemical building blocks - expanding the space of proteins that can be designed, engineered, and manufactured. Today, we are advancing a growing pipeline of programmes based on world-leading science, enabling the precise engineering of biology to create transformative medicines, materials and sustainable products.

 As a fast-growing biotech at the forefront of generative biology, we're building a team of exceptional people who share our ambition to redefine what's possible with biology.

Join us and help shape the future of biology.

What we are looking for:

We are seeking an experienced assay development scientist to lead the continued evolution of Constructive Bio's proprietary tRNA display platform. The role will focus on enhancing assay performance, throughput, automation and reproducibility while enabling the discovery and characterisation of novel orthogonal translation machinery.

You will be able to combine a deep expertise in molecular biology, nucleic acid chemistry and quantitative assay development with the ability to identify sources of assay variability, establish rigorous quality controls and develop scalable workflows.

* Experience with genotype-to-phenotype selection technologies such mRNA display, ribosome display, phage display or related directed evolution platforms is welcomed.
* Strong understanding of assay performance characteristics, including robustness, reproducibility, sensitivity, specificity, dynamic range and sources of experimental bias.
* Experience designing and implementing controls, standards, reference materials and quality metrics for quantitative biological assays.
* Experience analysing and interpreting complex biological datasets, including NGS-based and count-based screening data.
* Demonstrated ability to independently evaluate scientific evidence, challenge assumptions and make data-driven recommendations.
* Strong communication, documentation and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to work effectively across multidisciplinary teams.

Great to haves:

* Experience in genetic code expansion, aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases, translation systems, synthetic biology or tRNA biology.
* Experience with deep mutational scanning, library screening technologies or other massively parallel experimental platforms.
* Knowledge of physical-organic chemistry relevant to nucleic acid modification, RNA chemistry or assay development.
* Experience developing automated laboratory workflows and applying Design of Experiments (DoE) approaches to optimisation.
* Familiarity with high-throughput screening environments and laboratory scale-up activities.
* Experience establishing quality control frameworks and transferring assays between teams, operators or sites.

Other details:

* We are open-minded regarding the structure of this appointment and welcome discussions with exceptional candidates about permanent, contract, full-time or part-time arrangements. We are primarily focused on identifying the right expertise and experience to support the continued development of our platform.
* Our facilities are in Whittlesford, South Cambridgeshire. Given the hands-on nature of assay development and experimental work, you will be expected to work frequently on-site.

* Competitive salary
* Discretionary annual performance bonus

* Opportunity to be part of our employee long term incentive scheme
